en.greeting: Hi! Today we talk about the future: your plans, things you can see coming, and things already in your calendar. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Plans with going to
steps.text: Let's start with plans: things you have in your head now for later.
steps.body: Form: **am / is / are + going to + verb**: I'm going to cook. She's going to buy a car. Indonesian just says *saya akan / mau*, with no *be*, but English always needs **am / is / are**: not `I going to cook`. After **to**, the verb never changes (no -s, no -ing): `going to buys` is wrong. Here *going to* doesn't mean *pergi*: it just shows the future. Negative: **I'm not going to…** Question: **Are you going to…?**

pairs.en: I'm going to cook.
She's going to buy a car.
They're going to move to Bandung.
I'm not going to work tomorrow.
Are you going to study tonight?
What are you going to do?
next week
next year

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Two parts again: the right be, and the plain verb after to.

question.prompt: Dimas is saving money. His plan: a new motorbike. Complete: Next month Dimas ___ a new motorbike.
question.explanation: Dimas = he → **is**, then **going to** + the plain verb: **is going to buy**. `going to buy` has no be, and `buys` is wrong after to: the verb never changes there.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Now a negative plan. Where does **not** go?

question.solution: We aren't going to sell our house.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kami tidak akan menjual rumah kami.
question.explanation: Negative = **aren't** (are not) + going to + verb: We **aren't going to sell** our house. *Tidak akan* is just **not** after are: `We don't going to` is wrong.

steps.title: I can see it coming
steps.text: Going to has a second job: predictions.
steps.body: Use **going to** for a **prediction** (a guess about the future) when you can **see the reason now**: dark clouds → **It's going to rain.** A glass at the edge of the table → **It's going to fall.** In *It's going to rain*, **it** means nothing: English just needs a word at the start. Before words that aren't verbs (late, hot, tired) add **be**: **It's going to be a hot day**, not `going to hot`.

pairs.en: Look at the clouds!
It's going to rain.
Watch out!
That glass is going to fall.
It's going to be a hot day.
He's going to be tired.

steps.title: Listen and reply
steps.text: You're in a taxi with Rina. Press play and listen to her.

question.listen: Look at the traffic! The cars aren't moving.
options: Oh no. We going to be late.
Oh no. We're going to be late.
Oh no. We're going to late.
question.prompt: Your plane is at 3 p.m. It's 2:30, and you're still in the taxi. Listen to Rina, then choose your reply.
question.explanation: You can see the traffic now, so it's a prediction with **going to**. **Late** is not a verb, so add **be**: **We're going to be late.** `We going to` has no are, and `going to late` has no be.

steps.title: It's in my calendar
steps.text: Last part: things fixed with another person, like a meeting or a ticket.
steps.body: When a time (and often a place) is **fixed with another person**, English often uses the **present continuous** you know (**am / is / are + verb-ing**) with a **future time word**: I'm meeting Budi at 5. Without a time word it can mean *right now*. Indonesian *Besok saya ketemu Budi* tempts you to say `Tomorrow I meet Budi`, but *I meet* is for habits. Your own idea, nothing fixed with anyone? **Going to** is best.

pairs.en: I'm meeting Budi at the cafe at 5.
pairs.id: Saya ketemu Budi di kafe jam 5. (sudah janjian)

pairs.en: We're having dinner with Bu Ani on Saturday.
pairs.id: Kami makan malam bersama Bu Ani hari Sabtu.

pairs.en: Dimas is flying to Bali on Friday.
pairs.id: Dimas terbang ke Bali hari Jumat. (sudah ada tiket)

pairs.en: I'm playing badminton with Sari on Sunday.
pairs.id: Saya main bulu tangkis dengan Sari hari Minggu.

pairs.en: What are you doing this weekend?
pairs.id: Kamu ada acara apa akhir pekan ini?

pairs.en: tomorrow at 9

steps.title: Budi's week
steps.text: Here is Budi's calendar. Everything in it is fixed with other people.

timeline.title: Fixed in the calendar
timeline.caption: Today is Monday. He's meeting a client on Wednesday, he's having dinner with Sari on Friday, and he's taking the train to Bandung on Saturday.

steps.title: Now or later?
steps.text: Look for the time word.

question.prompt: It's Monday. Rina says: 'I'm flying to Medan on Thursday.' When is Rina flying to Medan?
question.explanation: **I'm flying** + **on Thursday** = a fixed future arrangement (she has a ticket). The time word shows it's not right now, and it's one trip, not a habit.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas is writing a message. Help him.

question.prompt: Dimas and Sari have a table for two at a restaurant at 7 tonight. Dimas texts a friend: 'Sorry, I can't play futsal tonight. ___ Sari at 7.'
question.explanation: It's fixed with Sari (time and place), so use the present continuous: **I'm meeting** Sari at 7. `I meet` is for habits, and `I meeting` has no am.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip the cards. Say the meaning before you check.

steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

tips: Never drop am / is / are: **I'm going to…**, not `I going to…`.
After **to**, the plain verb: **going to buy**, not `going to buys`.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more? This page has a short video and exercises. It's a bit above your level, so focus on going to and the present continuous.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita membicarakan masa depan: rencanamu, hal yang sudah kelihatan akan terjadi, dan acara yang sudah masuk kalender. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: Rencana dengan going to
steps.text: Kita mulai dari rencana: hal yang sudah ada di kepalamu sekarang untuk nanti.
steps.body: Bentuknya: **am / is / are + going to + kata kerja**: I'm going to cook. She's going to buy a car. Bahasa Indonesia cukup bilang *saya akan / mau* tanpa *be*, tapi bahasa Inggris selalu butuh **am / is / are**: bukan `I going to cook`. Setelah **to**, kata kerjanya tidak berubah (tanpa -s, tanpa -ing): `going to buys` salah. Di sini *going to* bukan berarti *pergi*: itu hanya penanda masa depan. Negatif: **I'm not going to…** Pertanyaan: **Are you going to…?**

pairs.en: I'm going to cook.
She's going to buy a car.
They're going to move to Bandung.
I'm not going to work tomorrow.
Are you going to study tonight?
What are you going to do?
next week
next year

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dua bagian lagi: be yang tepat, dan kata kerja dasar setelah to.

question.prompt: Dimas sedang menabung. Rencananya: motor baru. Lengkapi: Next month Dimas ___ a new motorbike.
question.explanation: Dimas = he → **is**, lalu **going to** + kata kerja dasar: **is going to buy**. `going to buy` tidak punya be, dan `buys` salah setelah to: kata kerjanya tidak pernah berubah di situ.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sekarang rencana dalam bentuk negatif. **Not** ditaruh di mana?

question.solution: We aren't going to sell our house.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kami tidak akan menjual rumah kami.
question.explanation: Negatif = **aren't** (are not) + going to + kata kerja: We **aren't going to sell** our house. *Tidak akan* cukup jadi **not** setelah are: `We don't going to` salah.

steps.title: Sudah kelihatan
steps.text: Going to punya tugas kedua: prediksi.
steps.body: Pakai **going to** untuk **prediksi** (tebakan tentang masa depan) kalau kamu **bisa melihat alasannya sekarang**: awan gelap → **It's going to rain.** Gelas di pinggir meja → **It's going to fall.** Dalam *It's going to rain*, **it** tidak ada artinya: bahasa Inggris hanya butuh kata di awal. Sebelum kata yang bukan kata kerja (late, hot, tired), tambahkan **be**: **It's going to be a hot day**, bukan `going to hot`.

pairs.en: Look at the clouds!
It's going to rain.
Watch out!
That glass is going to fall.
It's going to be a hot day.
He's going to be tired.

steps.title: Dengar dan jawab
steps.text: Kamu di taksi bersama Rina. Tekan play dan dengarkan dia.

question.listen: Look at the traffic! The cars aren't moving.
options: Oh no. We going to be late.
Oh no. We're going to be late.
Oh no. We're going to late.
question.prompt: Pesawatmu jam 3 sore. Sekarang jam 2.30 dan kamu masih di taksi. Dengarkan Rina, lalu pilih jawabanmu.
question.explanation: Kamu bisa melihat kemacetannya sekarang, jadi ini prediksi dengan **going to**. **Late** bukan kata kerja, jadi tambahkan **be**: **We're going to be late.** `We going to` tidak punya are, dan `going to late` tidak punya be.

steps.title: Sudah masuk kalender
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: hal yang sudah dijadwalkan dengan orang lain, seperti rapat atau tiket.
steps.body: Kalau waktunya (sering juga tempatnya) **sudah dijadwalkan dengan orang lain**, bahasa Inggris sering memakai **present continuous** yang sudah kamu kenal (**am / is / are + kata kerja-ing**) dengan **kata waktu masa depan**: I'm meeting Budi at 5. Tanpa kata waktu, artinya bisa *sekarang*. *Besok saya ketemu Budi* bikin kamu ingin bilang `Tomorrow I meet Budi`, padahal *I meet* untuk kebiasaan. Masih idemu sendiri, belum janjian dengan siapa pun? **Going to** paling pas.

pairs.en: I'm meeting Budi at the cafe at 5.
pairs.id: Saya ketemu Budi di kafe jam 5. (sudah janjian)

pairs.en: We're having dinner with Bu Ani on Saturday.
pairs.id: Kami makan malam bersama Bu Ani hari Sabtu.

pairs.en: Dimas is flying to Bali on Friday.
pairs.id: Dimas terbang ke Bali hari Jumat. (sudah ada tiket)

pairs.en: I'm playing badminton with Sari on Sunday.
pairs.id: Saya main bulu tangkis dengan Sari hari Minggu.

pairs.en: What are you doing this weekend?
pairs.id: Kamu ada acara apa akhir pekan ini?

pairs.en: tomorrow at 9

steps.title: Minggu Budi
steps.text: Ini kalender Budi. Semua acaranya sudah dijadwalkan dengan orang lain.

timeline.title: Sudah masuk kalender
timeline.caption: Hari ini Senin. He's meeting a client on Wednesday, he's having dinner with Sari on Friday, dan he's taking the train to Bandung on Saturday.

steps.title: Sekarang atau nanti?
steps.text: Cari kata waktunya.

question.prompt: Hari ini Senin. Rina bilang: 'I'm flying to Medan on Thursday.' Kapan Rina terbang ke Medan?
question.explanation: **I'm flying** + **on Thursday** = janji terjadwal di masa depan (dia sudah punya tiket). Kata waktunya menunjukkan bukan sekarang, dan ini satu perjalanan, bukan kebiasaan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas sedang menulis pesan. Bantu dia.

question.prompt: Dimas dan Sari sudah pesan meja untuk berdua di restoran jam 7 malam ini. Dimas mengirim pesan ke temannya: 'Sorry, I can't play futsal tonight. ___ Sari at 7.'
question.explanation: Sudah dijadwalkan dengan Sari (jam dan tempatnya), jadi pakai present continuous: **I'm meeting** Sari at 7. `I meet` untuk kebiasaan, dan `I meeting` tidak punya am.

steps.title: Ulasan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartunya. Sebutkan artinya sebelum kamu cek.
